subject.title: Make adaptive refresh agent-aware with explicit local activity consent

question: Should CodexBar ship plain Adaptive as the fresh-install default while retaining the documented markerless v0.1–v0.3 ambiguity, with local activity scanning available only through the separate explicitly consented agent-aware mode?
rationale: The latest owner-authored commit narrows the privacy boundary, but the owner’s July 17 review required an explicit decision on the production policy and the legacy-default tradeoff; automated review cannot choose that user-facing contract.

options.title: Approve the documented contract
options.body: Keep plain Adaptive as the fresh-install default, preserve five minutes for identifiable legacy-unset installs, and accept the documented markerless legacy ambiguity after exact-head proof and merge refresh.

options.title: Preserve five minutes by default
options.body: Keep the separate opt-in agent-aware mode but restore five minutes as the fresh-install default to eliminate the ambiguous legacy behavior change.

options.title: Park the cadence change
options.body: Retain only independently useful scanner hardening or consent groundwork and defer both Adaptive default and agent-aware policy rollout.

recommendation.title: Approve the documented contract
recommendation.body: Keep plain Adaptive as the fresh-install default, preserve five minutes for identifiable legacy-unset installs, and accept the documented markerless legacy ambiguity after exact-head proof and merge refresh.

likelyOwner.reason: The owner wrote the blocking contract review and authored the latest commit implementing the narrowed direction.
